messages:
OncallBot: :rotating_light: P0 alert — payment-queue error rate > 45% for the last 5m. Paging primary @Alex P. (see incident stub: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1891234567)
Alex P.: taking primary. I see spikes in 500s from worker pods. Maria, can you be secondary for the next 2h? I might need a quick swap if I have to escalate to infra.
Maria K.: I can cover as secondary for 2h. If you need a break, ping me and I’ll take the bridge. Quick note: CS already flagged 3 customers reporting timeouts.
Alex P.: thanks. quick triage notes — metrics dashboard: payment-queue latency up, kv-cache miss rate increased, and autoscaler hasn't added pods in last 10m. initial checks:

- check pods: use `kubectl -n payments get pods -l app=payment-queue`
- check logs: `kubectl -n payments logs <pod> -c worker --since=15m`
- check HPA: `kubectl -n payments describe hpa payment-queue`

Jamie L.: copying runbook pointers:
- primary runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/payment-queue-failure
- kv fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback
- rollout rollback play: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quick-rollbacks

Sanjay R.: if autoscaler is stuck, try a manual rollout restart and watch for pending pods: 
```
kubectl -n payments rollout restart deploy/payment-queue
kubectl -n payments get pods -w -l app=payment-queue
```
If pods are stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, check image pull errors and env config.

Alex P.: observed one pod in CrashLoopBackOff with OOMKilled. Increasing memory might help short term. I’m going to scale up manually to see if it relieves latency.

Luis T.: heads up — customers on Dedicated may not be affected the same; early impact seems highest on hosted tenant pool. CS: @maria_k can you confirm which orgs are impacted? list in incident doc.

Maria K.: confirmed—12 orgs with timeouts, 2 enterprise accounts hitting P1 thresholds. I updated the incident doc and notified CSEs. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1891234567/details

Alex P.: manual scale command I ran:
```
kubectl -n payments scale deploy payment-queue --replicas=12
```
Monitoring now. If latency drops in 3-5m, we’ll keep scaled and then work on root cause (possible memory pressure from a recent quantization change in worker). If not, plan B is rollback to previous image tag.

Jamie L.: rollback command if needed:
```
kubectl -n payments set image deploy/payment-queue payment-queue=registry.redwood/internal/payment-queue:20260214-rc1
```
Make sure to update the incident doc before executing. Use canary if unsure.

OncallBot: Reminder: to hand off primary role, run `/hand-off @username` or update the oncall rota in ops-rotations (link: https://redwood.internal/ops/rotations). If you are leaving for >15m, mark yourself as away in the channel.

Alex P.: quick checklist for whoever takes over:
- confirm primary/secondary in thread
- copy runbook links to incident doc
- execute scale/rollback with careful tagging
- notify CS for impacted customers and add note in incident timeline
- if KV miss rate remains high, follow kv-cache-fallback runbook (link above)

Maria K.: if Alex needs to escalate to infra or SRE, page oncall-sre and include the HPA and pod logs. Tagging @Jamie L. for any latency insight.

Alex P.: latency trending down after scale. Will watch 10m and then start a controlled rollback if memory pressure persists. Thanks all — leaving primary with Maria in 10m unless I need to re-enter.

Maria K.: acknowledged — I’ll be primary in 10m. Quick pointer for the handoff: add a short TL;DR in the incident doc with current actions and next steps so the next oncall picks up quickly.

Sanjay R.: added one more quick mitigation tip — if you see excessive GC in logs, bump `JAVA_OPTS` memory ratio or add `-XX:+UseG1GC` flags in the deploy config, but treat as temporary.

Luis T.: :thumbsup: Good notes. Also adding links to monitoring panels in doc: error-rate, latency-percentiles, kv-cache-miss.

OncallBot: auto-note — handoff scheduled: Alex P. -> Maria K. at 1891234580. If anything changes post-handoff, reply here.

Alex P.: handing off now. Primary: Maria K. Secondary: Jamie L. Incident doc updated with current state and commands executed. I’m available if needed.

Maria K.: taking primary. I’ll keep monitoring and will escalate if errors tick back up. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :white_check_mark:
